modules.title: Classes of Matrix Maps
modules.doc:
The bundled `MatrixMap`s: `HPMap`, `UnitalMap`, `TPMap`, `PMap`, and `CPMap`.
These are defined over the bare minimum rings (`Semiring` or `RCLike`, respectively).

The combinations `PTPMap` (positive trace-preserving), `CPTPMap`, and `CPUMap`
(CP unital maps) take ℂ as the default class.

The majority of quantum theory revolves around `CPTPMap`s, so those are explored more
thoroughly in their file CPTP.lean.

declarations.name: HPMap
declarations.doc: Hermitian-preserving linear maps.
declarations.statement:
structure HPMap extends MatrixMap dIn dOut 𝕜 where
  HP : MatrixMap.IsHermitianPreserving toLinearMap

declarations.name: UnitalMap
declarations.doc: Unital linear maps.
declarations.statement:
structure UnitalMap [DecidableEq dIn] [DecidableEq dOut]
    extends MatrixMap dIn dOut R where
  unital : MatrixMap.Unital toLinearMap

declarations.name: TPMap
declarations.doc: Trace-preserving linear maps.
declarations.statement:
structure TPMap [Fintype dIn] [Fintype dOut] extends MatrixMap dIn dOut R where
  TP : MatrixMap.IsTracePreserving toLinearMap

declarations.name: PMap
declarations.doc: Positive linear maps.
declarations.statement:
structure PMap [Fintype dIn] [Fintype dOut]
    extends HPMap dIn dOut 𝕜 where
  pos : MatrixMap.IsPositive toLinearMap
  HP := pos.IsHermitianPreserving

declarations.name: CPMap
declarations.doc: Completely positive linear maps.
declarations.statement:
structure CPMap [Fintype dIn] [Fintype dOut] [DecidableEq dIn]
    extends PMap dIn dOut 𝕜 where
  cp : MatrixMap.IsCompletelyPositive toLinearMap
  pos := cp.IsPositive

declarations.name: PTPMap
declarations.doc:
Positive trace-preserving linear maps. These includes all channels, but aren't
necessarily *completely* positive, see `CPTPMap`.
declarations.statement:
structure PTPMap [Fintype dIn] [Fintype dOut]
  extends PMap dIn dOut 𝕜, TPMap dIn dOut 𝕜

declarations.name: PUMap
declarations.doc:
Positive unital maps. These are important because they are the
dual to `PTPMap`: they are the most general way to map *observables*.
declarations.statement:
structure PUMap [Fintype dIn] [Fintype dOut] [DecidableEq dIn] [DecidableEq dOut]
  extends PMap dIn dOut 𝕜, UnitalMap dIn dOut 𝕜

declarations.name: CPTPMap
declarations.doc:
Completely positive trace-preserving linear maps. This is the most common
meaning of "channel", often described as "the most general physically realizable
quantum operation".
declarations.statement:
structure CPTPMap [Fintype dIn] [Fintype dOut] [DecidableEq dIn]
  extends PTPMap dIn dOut (𝕜 := 𝕜), CPMap dIn dOut 𝕜 where

modules.title: Completely Positive Trace Preserving maps
modules.doc:
A `CPTPMap` is a `ℂ`-linear map between matrices (`MatrixMap` is an alias), bundled with the facts
that it `IsCompletelyPositive` and `IsTracePreserving`. CPTP maps are typically regarded as the
"most general quantum operation", as they map density matrices (`MState`s) to density matrices. The
type `PTPMap`, for maps that are positive (but not necessarily completely positive) is also
declared.

A large portion of the theory is in terms of the Choi matrix (`MatrixMap.choi_matrix`), as the
positive-definiteness of this matrix corresponds to being a CP map. This is
[Choi's theorem on CP maps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choi%27s_theorem_on_completely_positive_maps).

This file also defines several important examples of, classes of, and operations on, CPTPMaps:
 * `compose`: Composition of maps
 * `id`: The identity map
 * `replacement`: The replacement channel that always outputs the same state
 * `prod`: Tensor product of two CPTP maps, with notation M₁ ⊗ M₂
 * `piProd`: Tensor product of finitely many CPTP maps (Pi-type product)
 * `of_unitary`: The CPTP map corresponding to a unitary operation `U`
 * `IsUnitary`: Predicate whether the map corresponds to any unitary
 * `purify`: Purifying a channel into a unitary on a larger Hilbert space
 * `complementary`: The complementary channel to its purification
 * `IsEntanglementBreaking`, `IsDegradable`, `IsAntidegradable`: Entanglement breaking, degradable
    and antidegradable channels.
 * `SWAP`, `assoc`, `assoc'`, `traceLeft`, `traceRight`: The CPTP maps corresponding to important
    operations on states. These correspond directly to `MState.SWAP`, `MState.assoc`,
    `MState.assoc'`, `MState.traceLeft`, and `MState.traceRight`.

declarations.name: CPTPMap.ofEquiv
declarations.doc:
Given a equivalence (a bijection) between the types d₁ and d₂, that is, if they're
the same dimension, then there's a CPTP channel for this. This is what we need for
defining e.g. the SWAP channel, which is 'unitary' but takes heterogeneous input
and outputs types (d₁ × d₂) and (d₂ × d₁).
declarations.statement: def ofEquiv (σ : dIn ≃ dOut) : CPTPMap dIn dOut

declarations.name: CPTPMap.ofEquiv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma ofEquiv_apply (σ : dIn ≃ dOut) (ρ : MState dIn) :
    ofEquiv σ ρ = ρ.relabel σ.symm

declarations.statement: lemma equiv_inverse (σ : dIn ≃ dOut)  : (ofEquiv σ) ∘ (ofEquiv σ.symm) = id (dIn := dOut)

declarations.name: CPTPMap.exists_purify
CPTPMap.purify
declarations.doc:
Every channel can be written as a unitary channel on a larger system. In general, if
the original channel was A→B, we may need to go as big as dilating the output system (the
environment) by a factor of A*B. One way of stating this would be that it forms an
isometry from A to (B×A×B). So that we can instead talk about the cleaner unitaries, we
say that this is a unitary on (A×B×B). The defining properties that this is a valid
purification comes are `purify_IsUnitary` and `purify_trace`. This means the environment
always has type `dIn × dOut`.

Furthermore, since we need a canonical "0" state on B in order to add with the input,
we require a typeclass instance [Inhabited dOut].
declarations.statement: def purify (Λ : CPTPMap dIn dOut) : CPTPMap (dIn × dOut × dOut) (dIn × dOut × dOut)

declarations.name: CPTPMap.purify_IsUnitary
declarations.statement: lemma purify_IsUnitary (Λ : CPTPMap dIn dOut) : Λ.purify.IsUnitary

declarations.name: CPTPMap.purify_trace
declarations.doc:
With a channel Λ : A → B, a valid purification (A×B×B)→(A×B×B) is such that:
 * Preparing the default ∣0⟩ state on two copies of B
 * Appending these to the input
 * Applying the purified unitary channel
 * Tracing out the two left parts of the output
is equivalent to the original channel. This theorem states that the channel output by `purify`
has this property.

declarations.name: CPTPMap.prep_append_map_entry
declarations.doc:
The Stinespring preparation `prep ∘ append` acts on a matrix entry by the Kronecker product
with the fixed pure state `|default⟩⟨default|` on `dOut × dOut`.
declarations.statement:
theorem prep_append_map_entry (X : Matrix dIn dIn ℂ)
    (a₁ : dIn) (b₁c₁ : dOut × dOut) (a₂ : dIn) (b₂c₂ : dOut × dOut) :
    let τ := MState.pure (Ket.basis (default : dOut × dOut))
    let zero_prep : CPTPMap Unit (dOut × dOut) := replacement τ
    let prep := (id ⊗ᶜᵖ zero_prep)
    let append : CPTPMap dIn (dIn × Unit) := CPTPMap.ofEquiv (Equiv.prodPUnit dIn).symm
    (prep ∘ₘ append).map X (a₁, b₁c₁) (a₂, b₂c₂) =
    X a₁ a₂ * τ.m b₁c₁ b₂c₂

modules.title: The Degradable Order
modules.doc:
We define the "degradable order" on channels, where M ≤ N if N can be degraded to M. This is a
scoped instance, because there are other reasonable orders on channels.

The degradable order is actually only a preorder, because channels that are degradable to each other
are not necessarily equal. (For instance, unitary channels are degradable to the identity and vice
versa.) It can compare channels of different output dimensions, but they must have the same input
dimension. For this reason the `DegradablePreorder` is parameterized by the channel input type.

One might hope that if this was defined on the quotient type of "channels up to unitary equivalence"
that it would become an order; but this is not the case. That is, there are channels `A → B` that
are degradable to each other, but cannot be degraded to each other by unitary operations. For
instance, let A be the replacement channel that goes to a mixed state, and B be a replacement
channel that goes to a pure state.

Technical notes: to model "channels of different output types", the preorder is on the Sigma type of
channels parameterized by their output type. And since the output type needs to be a Fintype and
DecidableEq, the argument is also a Sigma to bring this along.

declarations.name: DegradablePreorder
declarations.statement:
def DegradablePreorder (dIn : Type*) [Fintype dIn] [DecidableEq dIn] : Preorder
    (Σ dOut : (Σ t, Fintype t × DecidableEq t), let _ := dOut.snd.1; CPTPMap dIn dOut.fst)

modules.title: Linear maps of matrices
modules.doc:
This file works with `MatrixMap`s, that is, linear maps from square matrices to square matrices.
Although this is just a shorthand for `Matrix A A R →ₗ[R] Matrix B B R`, there are several
concepts that specifically make sense in this context.

 * `toMatrix` is the rectangular "transfer matrix", where matrix multiplication commutes with map
   composition.
 * `choi_matrix` is the square "Choi matrix", see `MatrixMap.choi_PSD_iff_CP_map` for example usage
 * `kron` is the Kronecker product of matrix maps
 * `IsTracePreserving` states the trace of the output is always equal to the trace of the input.

We provide simp lemmas for relating these facts, prove basic facts e.g. composition and identity,
and some facts about `IsTracePreserving` maps.

declarations.name: MatrixMap
declarations.doc: A `MatrixMap` is a linear map between squares matrices of size A to size B, over R.
declarations.statement: abbrev MatrixMap (A B R : Type*) [Semiring R]

declarations.name: MatrixMap.id
declarations.doc: Alias of LinearMap.id, but specifically as a MatrixMap.
declarations.statement: def id : MatrixMap A A R

declarations.name: MatrixMap.choi_matrix
declarations.doc:
Choi matrix of a given linear matrix map. Note that this is defined even for things that
aren't CPTP, it's just rarely talked about in those contexts. This is the inverse of
`MatrixMap.of_choi_matrix`. Compare with `MatrixMap.toMatrix`, which gives the transfer matrix.
declarations.statement: def choi_matrix (M : MatrixMap A B R) : Matrix (B × A) (B × A) R

declarations.name: MatrixMap.of_choi_matrix
declarations.doc:
Given the Choi matrix, generate the corresponding R-linear map between matrices as a
MatrixMap. This is the inverse of `MatrixMap.choi_matrix`.
declarations.statement: def of_choi_matrix (M : Matrix (B × A) (B × A) R) : MatrixMap A B R

declarations.name: MatrixMap.map_choi_inv
declarations.doc: Proves that `MatrixMap.of_choi_matrix` and `MatrixMap.choi_matrix` inverses.
declarations.statement: theorem map_choi_inv (M : Matrix (B × A) (B × A) R) : choi_matrix (of_choi_matrix M) = M

declarations.name: MatrixMap.choi_map_inv
declarations.doc: Proves that `MatrixMap.choi_matrix` and `MatrixMap.of_choi_matrix` inverses.
declarations.statement: theorem choi_map_inv (M : MatrixMap A B R) : of_choi_matrix (choi_matrix M) = M

declarations.name: MatrixMap.choi_matrix_inj
declarations.doc: The correspondence induced by `MatrixMap.of_choi_matrix` is injective.
declarations.statement: theorem choi_matrix_inj : Function.Injective (@choi_matrix A B R _ _)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.choi_equiv
declarations.doc: The linear equivalence between linear maps of matrices,and Choi matrices.
declarations.statement: def choi_equiv : MatrixMap A B R ≃ₗ[R] Matrix (B × A) (B × A) R

declarations.name: MatrixMap.toMatrix
declarations.doc:
The linear equivalence between MatrixMap's and transfer matrices on a larger space.
Compare with `MatrixMap.choi_matrix`, which gives the Choi matrix instead of the transfer matrix.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def toMatrix [Fintype B] : MatrixMap A B R ≃ₗ[R] Matrix (B × B) (A × A) R

declarations.name: MatrixMap.toMatrix_comp
declarations.doc: Multiplication of transfer matrices, `MatrixMap.toMatrix`, is equivalent to composition of maps.
declarations.statement: theorem toMatrix_comp [Fintype B] [Fintype C] [DecidableEq B] (M₁ : MatrixMap A B R) (M₂ : MatrixMap B C R) : toMatrix (M₂ ∘ₗ M₁) = (toMatrix M₂) * (toMatrix M₁)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.of_kraus
declarations.doc:
Construct a matrix map out of families of matrices M N : Σ → Matrix B A R
indexed by κ via X ↦ ∑ k : κ, (M k) * X * (N k)ᴴ
declarations.statement: def of_kraus (M N : κ → Matrix B A R) : MatrixMap A B R

declarations.name: MatrixMap.exists_kraus
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_kraus (Φ : MatrixMap A B R) :
    ∃ r : ℕ, ∃ (M N : Fin r → Matrix B A R), Φ = of_kraus M N

declarations.name: MatrixMap.submatrix
declarations.doc: The `MatrixMap` corresponding to applying a `submatrix` operation on each side.
declarations.statement: def submatrix (f : B → A) : MatrixMap A B R

declarations.name: MatrixMap.submatrix_id
declarations.statement: lemma submatrix_id : submatrix R _root_.id = id A R

declarations.name: MatrixMap.submatrix_comp
declarations.statement:
lemma submatrix_comp (f : C → B) (g : B → A) :
    submatrix R f ∘ₗ submatrix R g = submatrix R (g ∘ f)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.kron
declarations.doc:
The Kronecker product of MatrixMaps. Defined here using `TensorProduct.map M₁ M₂`, with
appropriate reindexing operations and `LinearMap.toMatrix`/`Matrix.toLin`. Notation `⊗ₖₘ`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def kron [CommSemiring R] (M₁ : MatrixMap A B R) (M₂ : MatrixMap C D R) : MatrixMap (A × C) (B × D) R

declarations.name: MatrixMap.kron_def
declarations.doc:
The extensional definition of the Kronecker product `MatrixMap.kron`, in terms of the entries of
its image.
declarations.statement:
theorem kron_def [CommSemiring R] (M₁ : MatrixMap A B R) (M₂ : MatrixMap C D R) (M : Matrix (A × C) (A × C) R) :
    (M₁ ⊗ₖₘ M₂) M (b₁, d₁) (b₂, d₂) = ∑ a₁, ∑ a₂, ∑ c₁, ∑ c₂,
      (M₁ (Matrix.single a₁ a₂ 1) b₁ b₂) * (M₂ (Matrix.single c₁ c₂ 1) d₁ d₂) * (M (a₁, c₁) (a₂, c₂))

declarations.name: MatrixMap.add_kron
declarations.statement: lemma add_kron (ML₁ ML₂ : MatrixMap A B R) (MR : MatrixMap C D R) : (ML₁ + ML₂) ⊗ₖₘ MR = ML₁ ⊗ₖₘ MR + ML₂ ⊗ₖₘ MR

declarations.name: MatrixMap.kron_add
declarations.statement: lemma kron_add (ML : MatrixMap A B R) (MR₁ MR₂ : MatrixMap C D R) : ML ⊗ₖₘ (MR₁ + MR₂) = ML ⊗ₖₘ MR₁ + ML ⊗ₖₘ  MR₂

declarations.name: MatrixMap.smul_kron
declarations.statement: lemma smul_kron (r : R) (ML : MatrixMap A B R) (MR : MatrixMap C D R) : (r • ML) ⊗ₖₘ MR = r • (ML ⊗ₖₘ MR)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.kron_smul
declarations.statement: lemma kron_smul (r : R) (ML : MatrixMap A B R) (MR : MatrixMap C D R) : ML ⊗ₖₘ (r • MR) = r • (ML ⊗ₖₘ MR)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.zero_kron
declarations.statement: lemma zero_kron (MR : MatrixMap C D R) : (0 : MatrixMap A B R) ⊗ₖₘ MR = 0

declarations.name: MatrixMap.kron_zero
declarations.statement: lemma kron_zero (ML : MatrixMap A B R) : ML ⊗ₖₘ (0 : MatrixMap C D R) = 0

declarations.name: MatrixMap.kron_id_id
declarations.statement: lemma kron_id_id : (id A R ⊗ₖₘ id B R) = id (A × B) R

declarations.name: MatrixMap.kron_comp_distrib
declarations.doc: For maps L₁, L₂, R₁, and R₂, the product (L₂ ∘ₗ L₁) ⊗ₖₘ (R₂ ∘ₗ R₁) = (L₂ ⊗ₖₘ R₂) ∘ₗ (L₁ ⊗ₖₘ R₁)
declarations.statement:
theorem kron_comp_distrib (L₁ : MatrixMap Dl₁ Dl₂ R) (L₂ : MatrixMap Dl₂ Dl₃ R) (R₁ : MatrixMap Dr₁ Dr₂ R)
    (R₂ : MatrixMap Dr₂ Dr₃ R) : (L₂ ∘ₗ L₁) ⊗ₖₘ (R₂ ∘ₗ R₁) = (L₂ ⊗ₖₘ R₂) ∘ₗ (L₁ ⊗ₖₘ R₁)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.kron_map_of_kron_state
declarations.doc:
The operational definition of the Kronecker product `MatrixMap.kron`, that it maps a Kronecker
product of inputs to the Kronecker product of outputs. It is the unique bilinear map doing so.
declarations.statement: theorem kron_map_of_kron_state [CommRing R] (M₁ : MatrixMap A B R) (M₂ : MatrixMap C D R) (MA : Matrix A A R) (MC : Matrix C C R) : (M₁ ⊗ₖₘ M₂) (MA ⊗ₖ MC) = (M₁ MA) ⊗ₖ (M₂ MC)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.choi_matrix_state_rep
declarations.statement:
lemma choi_matrix_state_rep {B : Type*} [Fintype B] [Nonempty A] (M : MatrixMap A B ℂ) :
    M.choi_matrix = (↑(Fintype.card (α := A)) : ℂ) • (M ⊗ₖₘ (LinearMap.id : MatrixMap A A ℂ)) (MState.pure (Ket.MES A)).m

declarations.name: MatrixMap.submatrix_kron_submatrix
declarations.statement:
lemma submatrix_kron_submatrix [CommSemiring R] (f : B → A) (g : D → C) :
    submatrix R f ⊗ₖₘ submatrix R g = submatrix R (Prod.map f g)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.submatrix_kron_id
declarations.statement:
lemma submatrix_kron_id [CommSemiring R] (f : B → A) :
    submatrix R f ⊗ₖₘ id C R = submatrix R (Prod.map f _root_.id)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.id_kron_submatrix
declarations.statement:
lemma id_kron_submatrix [CommSemiring R] (f : B → A) :
    id C R ⊗ₖₘ submatrix R f = submatrix R (Prod.map _root_.id f)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.piProd
declarations.doc:
Finite Pi-type tensor product of MatrixMaps. Defined as `PiTensorProduct.tprod` of the
underlying Linear maps. Notation `⨂ₜₘ[R] i, f i`, eventually.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def piProd (Λi : ∀ i, MatrixMap (dI i) (dO i) R) : MatrixMap (∀i, dI i) (∀i, dO i) R

declarations.name: MatrixMap.choi_matrix_piProd
declarations.statement:
lemma choi_matrix_piProd (Λi : ∀ i, MatrixMap (dI i) (dO i) R) :
    (MatrixMap.piProd Λi).choi_matrix =
      Matrix.reindex
        (Equiv.arrowProdEquivProdArrow ι dO dI)
        (Equiv.arrowProdEquivProdArrow ι dO dI)
        (Matrix.piProd (fun i => (Λi i).choi_matrix))

declarations.name: MatrixMap.piProd_comp
declarations.doc: Composition of `MatrixMap.piProd` maps distributes over the tensor product.
declarations.statement:
theorem piProd_comp
  {d₁ d₂ d₃ : ι → Type*}
  [∀ i, Fintype (d₁ i)] [∀ i, DecidableEq (d₁ i)]
  [∀ i, Fintype (d₂ i)] [∀ i, DecidableEq (d₂ i)]
  [∀ i, Fintype (d₃ i)] [∀ i, DecidableEq (d₃ i)]
  (Λ₁ : ∀ i, MatrixMap (d₁ i) (d₂ i) R) (Λ₂ : ∀ i, MatrixMap (d₂ i) (d₃ i) R) :
    piProd (fun i ↦ (Λ₂ i) ∘ₗ (Λ₁ i)) = (piProd Λ₂) ∘ₗ (piProd Λ₁)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.piProd_id
declarations.statement:
lemma piProd_id :
    piProd (fun i ↦ (LinearMap.id : MatrixMap (dI i) (dI i) R)) = LinearMap.id

modules.title: Pinching channels
modules.doc:
A pinching channel decoheres in the eigenspaces of a given state.
More precisely, given a state ρ, the pinching channel with respect to ρ is defined as
  E(σ) = ∑ Pᵢ σ Pᵢ
where the P_i are the projectors onto the i-th eigenspaces of ρ = ∑ᵢ pᵢ Pᵢ, with i ≠ j → pᵢ ≠ pⱼ.

TODO: Generalize to pinching with respect to arbitrary P(O)VM.

declarations.name: pinching_kraus
declarations.statement: def pinching_kraus (ρ : MState d) : spectrum ℝ ρ.m → HermitianMat d ℂ

declarations.name: pinching_kraus_commutes
declarations.statement:
lemma pinching_kraus_commutes (ρ : MState d) (i : spectrum ℝ ρ.m) :
    Commute (pinching_kraus ρ i).mat ρ.m

declarations.name: pinching_kraus_mul_self
declarations.statement:
lemma pinching_kraus_mul_self (ρ : MState d) (i : spectrum ℝ ρ.m) :
    (pinching_kraus ρ i).mat * ρ.m = i.val • pinching_kraus ρ i

declarations.name: finite_spectrum_inst
declarations.statement: instance finite_spectrum_inst (ρ : MState d) : Fintype (spectrum ℝ ρ.m)

declarations.name: pinching_kraus_orthogonal
declarations.statement:
lemma pinching_kraus_orthogonal (ρ : MState d) {i j : spectrum ℝ ρ.m} (h : i ≠ j) :
    (pinching_kraus ρ i).mat * (pinching_kraus ρ j).mat = 0

declarations.name: pinching_sq_eq_self
declarations.doc: The Kraus operators of the pinching channelare projectors: they square to themselves.
declarations.statement: theorem pinching_sq_eq_self (ρ : MState d) (k) : (pinching_kraus ρ k) ^ 2  = pinching_kraus ρ k

declarations.name: pinching_kraus_ortho
declarations.doc: The Kraus operators of the pinching channel are orthogonal projectors.
declarations.statement:
theorem pinching_kraus_ortho (ρ : MState d) (i j : spectrum ℝ ρ.m) :
    (pinching_kraus ρ i).mat * (pinching_kraus ρ j).mat = if i = j then (pinching_kraus ρ i).mat else 0

declarations.name: pinching_sum
declarations.statement: lemma pinching_sum (ρ : MState d) : ∑ k, pinching_kraus ρ k = 1

declarations.name: pinching_map
declarations.statement: def pinching_map (ρ : MState d) : CPTPMap d d ℂ

declarations.name: pinchingMap_apply_M
declarations.statement:
lemma pinchingMap_apply_M (σ ρ : MState d) : (pinching_map σ ρ).M =
  ⟨_, (MatrixMap.of_kraus_isCompletelyPositive
    (HermitianMat.mat ∘ pinching_kraus σ)).IsPositive.IsHermitianPreserving ρ.M.H⟩

declarations.name: pinching_eq_sum_conj
declarations.statement:
lemma pinching_eq_sum_conj (σ ρ : MState d) : (pinching_map σ ρ).M =
    ∑ k, (pinching_kraus σ k).mat * ρ.M * (pinching_kraus σ k).mat

declarations.name: pinching_commutes_kraus
declarations.statement:
lemma pinching_commutes_kraus (σ ρ : MState d) (i : spectrum ℝ σ.m) :
    Commute (pinching_map σ ρ).m (pinching_kraus σ i).mat

declarations.name: pinching_commutes
declarations.statement:
lemma pinching_commutes (ρ σ : MState d) :
    Commute (pinching_map σ ρ).m σ.m

declarations.name: pinching_self
declarations.statement: lemma pinching_self (ρ : MState d) : pinching_map ρ ρ = ρ

declarations.name: pinching_bound
declarations.doc:
Lemma 3.10 of Hayashi's book "Quantum Information Theory - Mathematical Foundations".
Also, Lemma 5 in https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0107004.
-- Used in (S60)
declarations.statement: theorem pinching_bound (ρ σ : MState d) : ρ.M ≤ (↑(Fintype.card (spectrum ℝ σ.m)) : ℝ) • (pinching_map σ ρ).M

declarations.name: ker_le_ker_pinching_of_PosDef
declarations.statement: lemma ker_le_ker_pinching_of_PosDef (ρ σ : MState d) (hpos : σ.m.PosDef) : σ.M.ker ≤ (pinching_map σ ρ).M.ker

declarations.name: pinching_idempotent
declarations.statement:
lemma pinching_idempotent (ρ σ : MState d) :
    (pinching_map σ) (pinching_map σ ρ) = (pinching_map σ ρ)

declarations.name: inner_cfc_pinching
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_cfc_pinching (ρ σ : MState d) (f : ℝ → ℝ) :
    ⟪ρ.M, (pinching_map σ ρ).M.cfc f⟫ = ⟪(pinching_map σ ρ).M, (pinching_map σ ρ).M.cfc f⟫

declarations.name: inner_cfc_pinching_right
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_cfc_pinching_right (ρ σ : MState d) (f : ℝ → ℝ) :
    ⟪(pinching_map σ ρ).M, σ.M.cfc f⟫ = ⟪ρ.M, σ.M.cfc f⟫

declarations.name: pinching_map_eq_sum_conj_hermitian
declarations.statement:
lemma pinching_map_eq_sum_conj_hermitian (σ ρ : MState d) :
    (pinching_map σ ρ).M = ∑ k, ρ.M.conj (pinching_kraus σ k).mat

declarations.name: pinching_map_ker_le
declarations.statement: lemma pinching_map_ker_le (ρ σ : MState d) : (pinching_map σ ρ).M.ker ≤ ρ.M.ker

declarations.name: pinching_kraus_ker_of_ne_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma pinching_kraus_ker_of_ne_zero {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    (σ : MState d) (v : d → ℂ) (hv : σ.m.mulVec v = 0)
    (k : spectrum ℝ σ.m) (hk : k.val ≠ 0) :
    (pinching_kraus σ k).mat *ᵥ v = 0

declarations.name: ker_le_ker_pinching_map_ker
declarations.statement:
lemma ker_le_ker_pinching_map_ker (ρ σ : MState d) (h : σ.M.ker ≤ ρ.M.ker) :
    σ.M.ker ≤ (pinching_map σ ρ).M.ker

declarations.name: pinching_pythagoras
declarations.doc: Exercise 2.8 of Hayashi's book "A group theoretic approach to Quantum Information".
declarations.statement:
theorem pinching_pythagoras (ρ σ : MState d) :
    𝐃(ρ‖σ) = 𝐃(ρ‖pinching_map σ ρ) + 𝐃(pinching_map σ ρ‖σ)

modules.title: Properties of Matrix Maps
modules.doc:
Building on `MatrixMap`s, this defines the properties: `IsTracePreserving`, `Unital`,
`IsHermitianPreserving`, `IsPositive` and `IsCompletelyPositive`. They have basic facts
such as closure under composition, addition, and scaling.

These are the *unbundled* versions, which just state the relevant properties of a given `MatrixMap`.
The bundled versions are `HPMap`, `UnitalMap`, `TPMap`, `PMap`, and `CPMap` respectively, given
in Bundled.lean.

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsTracePreserving
declarations.doc: A linear matrix map is *trace preserving* if trace of the output equals trace of the input.
declarations.statement: def IsTracePreserving (M : MatrixMap A B R) : Prop

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsTracePreserving_iff_trace_choi
declarations.doc: A map is trace preserving iff the partial trace of the Choi matrix is the identity.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsTracePreserving_iff_trace_choi [DecidableEq A] (M : MatrixMap A B R) : M.IsTracePreserving
    ↔ M.choi_matrix.traceLeft = 1

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsTracePreserving.apply_trace
declarations.doc:
Simp lemma: the trace of the image of a IsTracePreserving map is the same as the original
trace.
declarations.statement:
theorem apply_trace (h : M.IsTracePreserving) (ρ : Matrix A A R)
    : (M ρ).trace = ρ.trace

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsTracePreserving.trace_choi
declarations.doc: The trace of a Choi matrix of a TP map is the cardinality of the input space.
declarations.statement:
theorem trace_choi [DecidableEq A] (h : M.IsTracePreserving) :
    M.choi_matrix.trace = (Finset.univ (α := A)).card

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsTracePreserving.comp
declarations.doc: The composition of IsTracePreserving maps is also trace preserving.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp (h₁ : M.IsTracePreserving) (h₂ : M₂.IsTracePreserving) :
    IsTracePreserving (M₂ ∘ₗ M)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsTracePreserving.id
declarations.doc: The identity MatrixMap IsTracePreserving.
declarations.statement: theorem id : (id A R).IsTracePreserving

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsTracePreserving.unit_linear
declarations.doc: Unit linear combinations of IsTracePreserving maps are IsTracePreserving.

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsTracePreserving.kron
declarations.doc: The kronecker product of IsTracePreserving maps is also trace preserving.
declarations.statement:
theorem kron {M₁ : MatrixMap A B R} {M₂ : MatrixMap C D R} (h₁ : M₁.IsTracePreserving) (h₂ : M₂.IsTracePreserving) :
    (M₁ ⊗ₖₘ M₂).IsTracePreserving

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsTracePreserving.piProd
declarations.doc: The `MatrixMap.piProd` product of IsTracePreserving maps is also trace preserving.
declarations.statement:
theorem piProd {Λi : ∀ i, MatrixMap (dI i) (dO i) R} (h₁ : ∀ i, (Λi i).IsTracePreserving) :
    (MatrixMap.piProd Λi).IsTracePreserving

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsTracePreserving.of_kraus_isTracePreserving
declarations.doc:
The channel X ↦ ∑ k : κ, (M k) * X * (N k)ᴴ formed by Kraus operators M, N : κ → Matrix B A R
is trace-preserving if ∑ k : κ, (N k)ᴴ * (M k) = 1
declarations.statement:
theorem of_kraus_isTracePreserving
  (M N : κ → Matrix B A S)
  (hTP : (∑ k, (N k).conjTranspose * (M k)) = 1) :
  (MatrixMap.of_kraus M N).IsTracePreserving

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsTracePreserving.submatrix
declarations.doc: `MatrixMap.submatrix` is trace-preserving when the function is an equivalence.
declarations.statement: theorem submatrix (e : A ≃ B) : (MatrixMap.submatrix R e).IsTracePreserving

declarations.name: MatrixMap.Unital
declarations.doc: A linear matrix map is *unital* if it preserves the identity.
declarations.statement: def Unital (M : MatrixMap A B R) : Prop

declarations.name: MatrixMap.Unital.map_1
declarations.statement: lemma map_1 (h : M.Unital) : M 1 = 1

declarations.name: MatrixMap.Unital.id
declarations.doc: The identity `MatrixMap` is `Unital`.
declarations.statement: theorem id : (id A R).Unital

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsHermitianPreserving
declarations.doc: A linear matrix map is *Hermitian preserving* if it maps `IsHermitian` matrices to `IsHermitian`.
declarations.statement: def IsHermitianPreserving (M : MatrixMap A B R) : Prop

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsPositive
declarations.doc: A linear matrix map is *positive* if it maps `PosSemidef` matrices to `PosSemidef`.
declarations.statement: def IsPositive [Fintype A] [Fintype B] (M : MatrixMap A B R) : Prop

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsCompletelyPositive
declarations.doc:
A linear matrix map is *completely positive* if, for any integer n, the tensor product
with `I(n)` is positive.
declarations.statement: def IsCompletelyPositive [Fintype A] [Fintype B] [DecidableEq A] (M : MatrixMap A B R) : Prop

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsHermitianPreserving.id
declarations.doc: The identity MatrixMap IsHermitianPreserving.
declarations.statement: theorem id : (id A R).IsPositive

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsHermitianPreserving.comp
declarations.doc: The composition of IsHermitianPreserving maps is also Hermitian preserving.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp {M₁ : MatrixMap A B R} {M₂ : MatrixMap B C R}
    (h₁ : M₁.IsHermitianPreserving) (h₂ : M₂.IsHermitianPreserving) : IsHermitianPreserving (M₂ ∘ₗ M₁)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsPositive.IsHermitianPreserving
declarations.statement:
lemma IsHermitianPreserving {M : MatrixMap A B R}
    (hM : IsPositive M) : IsHermitianPreserving M

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsPositive.comp
declarations.doc: The composition of IsPositive maps is also positive.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp {M₁ : MatrixMap A B R} {M₂ : MatrixMap B C R} (h₁ : M₁.IsPositive)
    (h₂ : M₂.IsPositive) : IsPositive (M₂ ∘ₗ M₁)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsPositive.id
declarations.doc: The identity MatrixMap IsPositive.
declarations.statement: theorem id : (id A R).IsPositive

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsPositive.add
declarations.doc: Sums of IsPositive maps are IsPositive.
declarations.statement:
theorem add {M₁ M₂ : MatrixMap A B R} (h₁ : M₁.IsPositive) (h₂ : M₂.IsPositive) :
    (M₁ + M₂).IsPositive

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsPositive.smul
declarations.doc: Nonnegative scalings of IsPositive maps are IsPositive.
declarations.statement:
theorem smul {M : MatrixMap A B R} (hM : M.IsPositive) {x : R} (hx : 0 ≤ x) :
    (x • M).IsPositive

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsCompletelyPositive.of_Fintype
declarations.doc: Definition of a CP map, but with `Fintype T` in the definition instead of a `Fin n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem of_Fintype  {M : MatrixMap A B R} (h : IsCompletelyPositive M)
    (T : Type*) [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] :
    (M.kron (LinearMap.id : MatrixMap T T R)).IsPositive

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsCompletelyPositive.IsPositive
declarations.statement:
lemma IsPositive {M : MatrixMap A B R}
    (hM : IsCompletelyPositive M) : IsPositive M

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsCompletelyPositive.comp
declarations.doc: The composition of IsCompletelyPositive maps is also completely positive.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp [DecidableEq B] {M₁ : MatrixMap A B R} {M₂ : MatrixMap B C R} (h₁ : M₁.IsCompletelyPositive)
    (h₂ : M₂.IsCompletelyPositive) : IsCompletelyPositive (M₂ ∘ₗ M₁)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsCompletelyPositive.id
declarations.doc: The identity MatrixMap IsCompletelyPositive.
declarations.statement: theorem id : (id A R).IsCompletelyPositive

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsCompletelyPositive.add
declarations.doc: Sums of IsCompletelyPositive maps are IsCompletelyPositive.
declarations.statement:
theorem add {M₁ M₂ : MatrixMap A B R} (h₁ : M₁.IsCompletelyPositive) (h₂ : M₂.IsCompletelyPositive) :
    (M₁ + M₂).IsCompletelyPositive

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsCompletelyPositive.smul
declarations.doc: Nonnegative scalings of `IsCompletelyPositive` maps are `IsCompletelyPositive`.
declarations.statement:
theorem smul {M : MatrixMap A B R} (hM : M.IsCompletelyPositive) {x : R} (hx : 0 ≤ x) :
    (x • M).IsCompletelyPositive

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsCompletelyPositive.zero
declarations.doc: The zero map `IsCompletelyPositive`.
declarations.statement: theorem zero : (0 : MatrixMap A B R).IsCompletelyPositive

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsCompletelyPositive.finset_sum
declarations.doc: A finite sum of completely positive maps is completely positive.
declarations.statement:
theorem finset_sum {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {m : ι → MatrixMap A B R} (hm : ∀ i, (m i).IsCompletelyPositive) :
    (∑ i, m i).IsCompletelyPositive

declarations.name: MatrixMap.kron_kronecker_const
declarations.doc:
The map that takes M and returns M ⊗ₖ C, where C is positive semidefinite, is a completely
positive map.
declarations.statement:
theorem kron_kronecker_const {C : Matrix d d R} (h : C.PosSemidef) {h₁ h₂ : _} : IsCompletelyPositive
    (⟨⟨fun M => M ⊗ₖ C, h₁⟩, h₂⟩ : MatrixMap A (A × d) R)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.choi_of_kraus
declarations.statement:
lemma choi_of_kraus (K : κ → Matrix B A 𝕜) :
    (MatrixMap.of_kraus K K).choi_matrix = ∑ k, Matrix.vecMulVec (fun (x : B × A) => K k x.1 x.2) (fun (x : B × A) => star (K k x.1 x.2))

declarations.name: MatrixMap.conj
declarations.doc: The linear map of conjugating a matrix by another, `x → y * x * yᴴ`.
declarations.statement: def _root_.MatrixMap.conj (y : Matrix B A R) : MatrixMap A B R

declarations.name: MatrixMap.conj_isPositive
declarations.statement: lemma conj_isPositive (M : Matrix B A 𝕜) : (conj M).IsPositive

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsPositive_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma IsPositive_sum {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (f : ι → MatrixMap A B ℂ) (h : ∀ i, (f i).IsPositive) :
    (∑ i, f i).IsPositive

declarations.name: MatrixMap.of_kraus_isPositive
declarations.statement:
lemma of_kraus_isPositive (K : κ → Matrix B A ℂ) :
    (of_kraus K K).IsPositive

declarations.name: MatrixMap.conj_kron
declarations.statement:
lemma conj_kron (M : Matrix B A 𝕜) (N : Matrix D C 𝕜) [DecidableEq C] :
    conj M ⊗ₖₘ conj N = conj (M ⊗ₖ N)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.congruence_one_eq_id
declarations.statement: lemma congruence_one_eq_id : conj (1 : Matrix A A ℂ) = MatrixMap.id A ℂ

declarations.name: MatrixMap.congruence_CP
declarations.statement: lemma congruence_CP {A B : Type*} [Fintype A] [Fintype B] [DecidableEq A] [DecidableEq B] (M : Matrix B A 𝕜) : (conj M).IsCompletelyPositive

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsCompletelyPositive_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma IsCompletelyPositive_sum {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (f : ι → MatrixMap A B ℂ) (h : ∀ i, (f i).IsCompletelyPositive) :
    (∑ i, f i).IsCompletelyPositive

declarations.name: MatrixMap.of_kraus_eq_sum_conj
declarations.statement:
lemma of_kraus_eq_sum_conj (K : κ → Matrix B A 𝕜) :
    of_kraus K K = ∑ k, conj (K k)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.of_kraus_CP
declarations.statement: lemma of_kraus_CP (K : κ → Matrix B A 𝕜) : (of_kraus K K).IsCompletelyPositive

declarations.name: MatrixMap.exists_kraus_of_choi_PSD
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_kraus_of_choi_PSD
    (C : Matrix (B × A) (B × A) 𝕜) (hC : C.PosSemidef) :
    ∃ (K : (B × A) → Matrix B A 𝕜), C = (MatrixMap.of_kraus K K).choi_matrix

declarations.name: MatrixMap.choi_matrix_eq_map_proj
declarations.statement:
lemma choi_matrix_eq_map_proj (M : MatrixMap A B R) :
    M.choi_matrix = (M ⊗ₖₘ MatrixMap.id A R) (Matrix.vecMulVec (fun (x : A × A) => if x.1 = x.2 then 1 else 0) (fun (x : A × A) => star (if x.1 = x.2 then 1 else 0)))

declarations.name: MatrixMap.choi_PSD_iff_CP_map
declarations.doc: Choi's theorem on completely positive maps: A map `IsCompletelyPositive` iff its Choi Matrix is PSD.
declarations.statement:
theorem choi_PSD_iff_CP_map (M : MatrixMap A B R) :
    M.IsCompletelyPositive ↔ M.choi_matrix.PosSemidef

declarations.name: MatrixMap.conj_eq_mulRightLinearMap_comp_mulRightLinearMap
declarations.statement:
lemma conj_eq_mulRightLinearMap_comp_mulRightLinearMap (y : Matrix B A R) :
    conj y = mulRightLinearMap B R y.conjTranspose ∘ₗ mulLeftLinearMap A R y

declarations.name: MatrixMap.conj_isCompletelyPositive
declarations.doc: The act of conjugating (not necessarily by a unitary, just by any matrix at all) is completely positive.
declarations.statement: theorem conj_isCompletelyPositive (M : Matrix B A R) : (conj M).IsCompletelyPositive

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsCompletelyPositive.submatrix
declarations.doc: `MatrixMap.submatrix` is completely positive
declarations.statement: theorem IsCompletelyPositive.submatrix (f : B → A) : (MatrixMap.submatrix R f).IsCompletelyPositive

declarations.name: MatrixMap.of_kraus_isCompletelyPositive
declarations.doc:
The channel X ↦ ∑ k : κ, (M k) * X * (M k)ᴴ formed by Kraus operators M : κ → Matrix B A R
is completely positive
declarations.statement:
theorem of_kraus_isCompletelyPositive (M : κ → Matrix B A R) :
    (of_kraus M M).IsCompletelyPositive

declarations.name: MatrixMap.choi_of_kraus_R
declarations.doc: The Choi matrix of a map in symmetric Kraus form is a sum of rank-1 projectors.
declarations.statement:
theorem choi_of_kraus_R [DecidableEq A] (K : κ → Matrix B A 𝕜) :
    (of_kraus K K).choi_matrix = ∑ k, Matrix.vecMulVec (fun (x : B × A) => K k x.1 x.2) (fun (x : B × A) => star (K k x.1 x.2))

declarations.name: MatrixMap.choi_eq_kron_id_apply_choi_id
declarations.statement:
lemma choi_eq_kron_id_apply_choi_id (M : MatrixMap A B R) :
    M.choi_matrix = (M ⊗ₖₘ MatrixMap.id A R) ((MatrixMap.id A R).choi_matrix)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.choi_id_is_PSD
declarations.statement:
lemma choi_id_is_PSD {A R : Type*} [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A] [RCLike R] :
    (MatrixMap.id A R).choi_matrix.PosSemidef

declarations.name: MatrixMap.is_CP_implies_choi_PSD
declarations.statement:
lemma is_CP_implies_choi_PSD {A B R : Type*} [Fintype A] [Fintype B] [DecidableEq A] [DecidableEq B] [RCLike R] (M : MatrixMap A B R) (hCP : M.IsCompletelyPositive) :
    M.choi_matrix.PosSemidef

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsCompletelyPositive.exists_kraus
declarations.statement:
lemma IsCompletelyPositive.exists_kraus (Φ : MatrixMap A B R) (hCP : Φ.IsCompletelyPositive) :
    ∃ (M : (B × A) → Matrix B A R), Φ = of_kraus M M

declarations.name: MatrixMap.cp_subunital_kadison_schwarz
declarations.doc: Kadison-Schwarz for completely positive subunital matrix maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma cp_subunital_kadison_schwarz {M : MatrixMap A B ℂ} [DecidableEq B]
    (hM : M.IsCompletelyPositive) (hM1 : M 1 ≤ (1 : Matrix B B ℂ))
    (X : Matrix A A ℂ) :
    (M X)ᴴ * M X ≤ M (Xᴴ * X)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.positive_subunital_norm_apply_le
declarations.doc: A positive subunital matrix map is contractive on positive inputs.
declarations.statement:
theorem positive_subunital_norm_apply_le {M : MatrixMap A B ℂ} [DecidableEq B]
    (hM : M.IsPositive) (hM1 : M 1 ≤ (1 : Matrix B B ℂ))
    {X : Matrix A A ℂ} (hX : 0 ≤ X) :
    ‖M X‖ ≤ ‖X‖

declarations.name: MatrixMap.cp_subunital_opNorm_le_one
declarations.doc: A completely positive subunital matrix map is contractive in operator norm.
declarations.statement:
theorem cp_subunital_opNorm_le_one {M : MatrixMap A B ℂ} [DecidableEq B]
    (hM : M.IsCompletelyPositive) (hM1 : M 1 ≤ (1 : Matrix B B ℂ))
    (X : Matrix A A ℂ) :
    ‖M X‖ ≤ ‖X‖

declarations.name: MatrixMap.kron_of_kraus
declarations.doc: The Kronecker product of two Kraus maps is the Kraus map of the Kronecker products of the operators.
declarations.statement:
theorem kron_of_kraus {A B C D R : Type*} [Fintype A] [Fintype B] [Fintype C] [Fintype D]
    [DecidableEq A] [DecidableEq C] [CommSemiring R] [StarRing R] [SMulCommClass R R R]
    {κ ι : Type*} [Fintype κ] [Fintype ι]
    (M : κ → Matrix B A R) (N : ι → Matrix D C R) :
    of_kraus M M ⊗ₖₘ of_kraus N N =
    of_kraus (fun (k : κ × ι) => M k.1 ⊗ₖ N k.2) (fun k => M k.1 ⊗ₖ N k.2)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsCompletelyPositive.kron
declarations.doc: The Kronecker product of IsCompletelyPositive maps is also completely positive.
declarations.statement:
theorem kron {D : Type*} [DecidableEq C] [Fintype D] {M₁ : MatrixMap A B R} {M₂ : MatrixMap C D R}
    (h₁ : M₁.IsCompletelyPositive) (h₂ : M₂.IsCompletelyPositive) : IsCompletelyPositive (M₁ ⊗ₖₘ M₂)

declarations.name: MatrixMap.IsCompletelyPositive.piProd
declarations.doc: The `MatrixMap.piProd` product of IsCompletelyPositive maps is also completely positive.
declarations.statement:
theorem piProd {Λi : ∀ i, MatrixMap (dI i) (dO i) R} (h₁ : ∀ i, (Λi i).IsCompletelyPositive) :
    IsCompletelyPositive (MatrixMap.piProd Λi)
